acme-ci: Hey @support, our CI started failing fetching a dependency after the vendor pushed a v2 tag. `go get github.com/vendor/mypkg@v2.0.0` now errors with 'unknown revision v2.0.0'. Repro steps and output below.

support: Can you paste `go env` and the exact `go get` output (copy/paste) and a link to the repo?

acme-ci: Sure — minimal repro below. Repo: https://github.com/vendor/mypkg 
```
$ go env
GO111MODULE="on"
GOOS="linux"
GOARCH="amd64"
GOMOD=/home/runner/work/app/app/go.mod
GOPROXY=https://proxy.golang.org,direct
```
```
$ go get github.com/vendor/mypkg@v2.0.0
go: finding github.com/vendor/mypkg v2.0.0
go: github.com/vendor/mypkg@v2.0.0: unknown revision v2.0.0
```
I also ran `git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/vendor/mypkg.git` and v2.0.0 is present.

mike.eng: :eyes: If the tag exists but `go` can't find the revision, often the module's declared path inside go.mod doesn't match the v2 import path. Can you show the tagged tree's go.mod?

acme-ci: Checked out the v2 tag and cat'd go.mod: `module github.com/vendor/mypkg` (no `/v2`).

bob.eng: Bingo — that's the classic v2 module path mismatch. For Go modules >=v2 the module path must include the major as a suffix (e.g., `github.com/vendor/mypkg/v2`) otherwise consumers importing `.../v2` won't resolve. The tag exists but the module metadata doesn't match what the proxy expects.

support: What's the recommended fix / mitigation for customers?

bob.eng: Two options:
1) Vendor should update module path in the repo (go.mod -> `module github.com/vendor/mypkg/v2`) and cut a new v2.0.1 tag that points at that commit. That's the correct fix.
2) Workaround for consumers: add a replace in your go.mod to point the v2 import to the non-/v2 module until vendor fixes upstream. Example (consumer go.mod):
```
replace github.com/vendor/mypkg/v2 => github.com/vendor/mypkg v0.0.0-00010101000000-000000000000
```
You can generate the pseudo-version by running `git ls-remote` or using the commit hash: e.g. `replace github.com/vendor/mypkg/v2 => github.com/vendor/mypkg v0.0.0-20231105-abcdef123456`

mike.eng: Also try `GOPROXY=direct go get github.com/vendor/mypkg@v2.0.0` locally — if that still fails with unknown revision but `git ls-remote` sees the tag, it confirms metadata mismatch rather than a transient proxy issue.

acme-ci: Thanks — will try the replace workaround and ping the vendor to retag. Any chance Redwood support can reach out to the vendor? This is blocking our release.

support-bot: Created ticket INC-2345 — Escalated to Eng Platform. Assigned: bob.eng.

bob.eng: I'll reach out to the vendor contact and include repro + suggested fix. For now the replace should unblock CI. If you paste your go.mod I can suggest the exact `replace` line. :thumbsup:

acme-ci: Pasted privately. Trying workaround now. Thanks everyone! :pray:
